text: If you walk into a bank and ask for $1 million in cash, right now, will they hand it over?
Mike tries it. The teller opens his drawer. Not even close.
He checks the vault too. Still not enough.
His account says one million dollars. But the cash? It isn't in this building.
Most of the money in your account isn't paper at all. It's a number on a screen.
A branch only keeps the cash it expects to need. So the teller calls the manager.
Mike gets angry. It's his money. The manager just nods. You'll get it. Just not today.
Then he opens a form. For cash over ten thousand dollars, the bank reports it to the government.
Automatically. It's routine, not an accusation.
So where is the money? Banks order it from the Federal Reserve, and armored trucks carry it.
Mike leaves with nothing. Banks often ask for a day or two of notice.
Day one. Nothing. Day two. His phone rings.
Then the truck arrives. Ten thousand hundred-dollar bills. About twenty-two pounds.
A stack almost four feet tall. And it all fits in one backpack.
So did Mike get his million? Yes. After the wait.
He walks out with a backpack worth a million dollars.
But here's the part that surprises people. The government already knew.
Would you carry a million in cash? Yes or no?
